2017 Jiefang Daily interview.basis: The hotel reception office identifies its historic No. 4 as the former residence of Yao Naichi and describes the split levels. The article gives 1948. Number 7 and the later guest-room addition are separately identified.

2017 syndication.limit: The archival garden-room picture shows earlier stained glass and furniture; no date of exposure is stated. A 2017 publication date is used for the outdoor image.

2019 Wenhui architecture article.identification: Caption identifies an exterior and interior pair as the Yao Residence. A separate image immediately before the pair depicts Fallingwater in Pennsylvania. The preceding American example is excluded.

2020 Shanghai heritage account.source_of_article: 上海老底子，转述上海长宁及《凝固的传奇—程家桥历史文化风情掠影》
2020 Shanghai heritage account.same_view: The exterior photograph is the same camera position as the 2017 syndication; it is a cross-reference, not a third station.

secondary chronology.limit: 1946 in the encyclopedia infobox differs from the 1948 date in the Jiefang Daily interview. The model records the postwar date range, without an inference about commencement or completion.

geometry_rights: The numerical building geometry and the generated renders are original MIT-licensed work. No publisher has granted reuse of these photographs here. External image files, press layouts and aerial crops are absent from the model, source and gallery.
